name: Mazda
overview: Renowned for innovative engineering, rotary-powered motorsport legends, and stylish consumer favourites. Mazda has consistently stood as Australia's second best-selling automotive marque for over two decades.
australian_history:
Mazda vehicles first reached Australian shores in 1959 through independent distributors, with the tiny R360 rear-engine coupe and light commercial utility models. In 1966, the Mazda 1000/1200 Familia arrived, establishing Mazda's reputation for mechanical sophistication.

The pivotal chapter in Mazda's Australian heritage began in 1969 with the rotary engine revolution. Following the R100 coupe, Mazda introduced the Capella Rotary (RX-2) in 1970, the RX-3 in 1971, and the RX-4 in 1973. Australian motorsport legend Allan Moffat forged the RX-3 into an iconic touring car weapon, famously challenging the V8 Holden Toranas and Ford Falcons at Mount Panorama, Bathurst. The rotary legend culminated with three generations of the RX-7 sports car (1979-2002); Moffat won the Australian Touring Car Championship in 1983 in an RX-7, and Allan Horsley's Mazda Motorsport skunkworks built the world-exclusive, twin-turbo RX-7 SP in Melbourne to win the Eastern Creek and Bathurst 12 Hour endurance races in 1995.

In the mainstream market, Mazda forged a deep alliance with Ford Australia throughout the 1980s and 1990s. The front-wheel-drive Mazda 323 (BD/BF) and 626 (GC/GD) formed the engineering foundation for the locally built Ford Laser, Meteor, and Telstar, which dominated Australian sales charts.

In 1989, Mazda introduced the MX-5 (NA), a lightweight rear-wheel-drive roadster that single-handedly revitalized the open-top sports car segment in Australia and worldwide. In 1992, Mazda launched its luxury Eunos sub-brand in Australia, showcasing advanced engineering like the world's first Miller-cycle engine in the Eunos 800.

The modern era began in 2002 with Mazda's emotive 'Zoom-Zoom' brand renaissance. The Mazda6 (2002) and Mazda3 (2004) set new standards for design, build quality, and driving dynamics in their respective classes. In 2011 and 2012, the Mazda3 achieved the extraordinary feat of becoming Australia's #1 selling car outright, unseating the Holden Commodore. In 2012, the CX-5 introduced Skyactiv lightweight chassis and powertrain technology, becoming Australia's favourite private SUV for years. Today, Mazda Australia remains headquartered in Mulgrave, Victoria, backed by a nationwide dealer network.

626-mazda6.name: 626 / Mazda6
626-mazda6.overview: The Mazda 626 and its successor the Mazda6 served as Australia's benchmark mid-size Japanese passenger car for 45 years. From the 1983 Wheels Car of the Year winning front-wheel drive 626 GC to the ferocious 190kW Mazda6 MPS turbocharged all-wheel-drive performance hero, it balanced executive styling with dynamic driver engagement.
626-mazda6.australian_market_notes: First imported as the rear-drive 626 CB in 1979, the model soared to acclaim with the 1983 GC series, which took Wheels Car of the Year. In 2002, the nameplate reinvented itself as the sleek Mazda6 (GG), winning universal accolades. In 2005, Mazda unleashed the Mazda6 MPS with a 2.3L turbo engine and active-torque AWD to rival Subaru's Liberty GT. Production concluded in 2024 with the 20th Anniversary Edition.

rx-3-808.name: RX-3 / 808
rx-3-808.overview: The Mazda RX-3 (Savanna) and its reciprocating-piston sister the Mazda 808 (Grand Familia) are iconic pillars of Australian motorsport history and Japanese performance folklore. Famed for taking the fight directly to Holden Torana GTR XU-1s and Ford Falcon GT-HOs at Mount Panorama Bathurst, the RX-3's screaming twin-rotor Wankel rotary engine won legions of fanatical followers.
rx-3-808.australian_market_notes: Introduced in March 1972, the RX-3 was sold alongside the cheaper, conventional four-cylinder 808. In motorsport, the RX-3 proved an unbeatable giant-killer in the under-3.0-litre class at the Bathurst 1000, claiming a historic 1st, 2nd, and 3rd in class in 1975 led by Don Holland. Surviving authentic RX-3 Coupes command extraordinary auction values across Australia today.

rx-7.name: RX-7
rx-7.overview: The Mazda RX-7 is a rotary-powered sports car legend with deep Australian motorsport roots. From Allan Moffat's ATCC championship and Bathurst battles in the 1980s to Mazda Motorsport's Australian-exclusive RX-7 SP winning the Bathurst 12 Hour in 1995.
rx-7.australian_market_notes: First imported in 1979, the RX-7 proved the reliability and racing potential of Felix Wankel's rotary design. The Series 1-3 dominated touring cars. bt-50.name: BT-50
bt-50.overview: The Mazda BT-50 has been an Australian tradie, touring, and towing mainstay across three generations, moving from a Ford Ranger twin with 3.2L 5-cylinder power to an Isuzu D-Max platform with the 3.0L 4JJ3 turbo-diesel.
bt-50.australian_market_notes: Replacing the Bravo in 2006, the BT-50 carved out a unique market position in Australia by offering Zoom-Zoom design and car-like ergonomics alongside 3.5-tonne towing and rugged 4WD capability. The UP/UR generation featured the unique 5-cylinder diesel, while the TF generation brought Australian-exclusive flagship editions like the Thunder.

generations.summary: Co-developed on the Ford T6 platform with the PX Ranger, famous for its muscular 3.2L 5-cylinder turbo-diesel generating 147kW and 470Nm.

engines.name: Mazda MZ-CD 3.2L 5-Cylinder Diesel
engines.notes: Renowned for deep 5-cylinder torque and heavy 3,500kg towing capability.

rx-8.name: RX-8
rx-8.overview: 4-door, 4-seat rotary sports coupe with rear suicide freestyle doors and the naturally aspirated RENESIS engine.

generations.summary: RENESIS 13B-MSP naturally aspirated rotary revving to 9000rpm (170kW-177kW); Base, Luxury, and GT.

121.overview: Quirky, beloved city car, famous in Australia for the DB 'Bubble' sedan and canvas 'Fun-top' roof.

generations.summary: 1.3L B3 engine, boxy packaging, co-developed with Ford Festiva.
1.3L and 1.5L engines, distinctive rounded jellybean styling and canvas sunroof.
Tall-boy hatchback packaging, 1.3L and 1.5L engines, succeeded by Mazda2.

mazda2.name: Mazda2
mazda2.overview: Fun-to-drive, stylish light car that has been an Australian small-car mainstay for over two decades.

generations.summary: 1.5L ZY-VE engine 82kW, tall mini-MPV profile; Neo, Maxx, and Genki.
Gram-strategy lightweight chassis (100kg lighter), 1.5L MZR engine, Wheels COTY 2007.
KODO design, Skyactiv-G 1.5L engine (79kW-82kW), G-Vectoring Control; Pure, Evolve, GT.

323.overview: Long-running small car range that cemented Mazda in Australia; platform twin to the Australian Ford Laser.

generations.summary: Rear-wheel drive, 1.3L and 1.4L engines, hatch with folding rear seat.
Switch to FWD, 1.3L and 1.5L engines; Australian Wheels COTY 1980.
1.6L B6 engine, introduced turbo AWD variants in Japan; SS and Deluxe trims.
Pop-up headlights on Astina 5-door, 1.6L and 1.8L DOHC engines; huge Australian cult status.
Hardtop doors, 1.8L BP and smooth 2.0L KF-DE V6 engine in Astina V6.
1.6L ZM-DE, 1.8L FP-DE, and 2.0L FS-DE in Astina SP20; final 323 before Mazda3.

626.overview: Refined Japanese mid-size car that challenged European competitors and shared DNA with the Ford Telstar.

generations.summary: Rear-wheel drive, 2.0L MA engine, comfortable ride, Wheels COTY runner-up.
Switch to FWD, 2.0L FE engine, electronic adjustable suspension (EVCS); Wheels COTY 1983.
2.2L F2 engine, optional 4WS (four-wheel steering) and turbo variants.
Sleek aerodynamic curves, 2.0L FS and smooth 2.5L KL-DE V6; Cronos architecture.
2.0L FS-DE engine, spacious practical cabin; succeeded by Mazda6 in 2002.

mazda6.name: Mazda6
mazda6.overview: Dynamic mid-size sports sedan and wagon that spearheaded Mazda's 'Zoom-Zoom' brand rebirth in Australia.

generations.summary: 2.3L MZR engine 122kW, double-wishbone front suspension; 190kW AWD MPS turbo in 2005.
2.5L L5-VE petrol and 2.2L MZR-CD turbodiesel; Classic, Luxury, Luxury Sports.
KODO styling, Skyactiv-G 2.5L, 2.2L twin-turbo diesel, and 170kW 2.5L Turbo (Atenza).

cx-3.name: CX-3
cx-3.overview: Perennial best-seller in the Australian light SUV category, based on the Mazda2 platform.

generations.summary: 2.0L Skyactiv-G petrol (110kW) and 1.5L/1.8L diesel; Neo, Maxx, sTouring, Akari.

cx-30.name: CX-30
cx-30.overview: Sleek coupe-crossover bridging the gap between the CX-3 and CX-5, built on the Mazda3 architecture.

generations.summary: 2.0L G20, 2.5L G25, and Skyactiv-X mild hybrid; Pure, Evolve, Touring, Astina.

cx-7.name: CX-7
cx-7.overview: Sporty crossover powered originally by the Mazda3 MPS turbo engine, an early precursor to the modern medium SUV boom.

generations.summary: 2.3L Turbo MZR 175kW AWD, later 2.5L naturally aspirated FWD and 2.2L diesel.

cx-8.name: CX-8
cx-8.overview: Narrower 7-seat family SUV blending CX-5 packaging with three-row capability, highly popular in diesel AWD.

generations.summary: 2.2L twin-turbo diesel and 2.5L petrol; Sport, Touring, GT, Asaki.

cx-9.name: CX-9
cx-9.overview: Spacious full-size 7-seat family SUV that won Wheels Car of the Year in 2008 and 2017 across two generations.

generations.summary: 3.7L MZI V6 engine 204kW, 6-speed auto, FWD and AWD; Wheels COTY 2008.
2.5L Skyactiv-G Turbo 170kW/420Nm, premium cabin; Wheels COTY 2017.

cx-60.name: CX-60
cx-60.overview: Mazda's premium push with rear-drive longitudinal architecture, inline-6 turbo engines, and plug-in hybrid options.

generations.summary: 3.3L Turbo Inline-6 petrol (209kW), 3.3L Inline-6 diesel (187kW), and 2.5L PHEV (241kW).
